notes.title: Release Date Announced
notes.notes:
Hey there slugs!

We're thrilled to announce the release of Turf Wars - A Snail Escape. Mark your calendars for November 30th, 2023. Dive into a world where snails aren't just slow-moving garden creatures, but agile slime-shooting warriors!🐌

All of the late nights, the brainstorming, the countless play-tests... it's all been for this moment. And we can't wait for you to experience the magic at the unbeatable price of $5.99 USD (or equivalent in your currency).

Here is some facts on the launch version on the game

 Supported languages: English, but it's gameplay focus game so don't worry if it isnt your preferred language
 Supported controllers: You can use both Keyboard/Mouse and any controller you might have.
 Number of players: It's a single player experience only
 Expected length: It's a roguelike so it all depends on you. There will be 5 areas with 5 unique bosses, 47 different enemies and 21 different items that can be upgrades in many ways. You can also replay the game on hard and ultra mode once you have beaten the game once. 
 I'm sure I missed some important info, so feel free to drop me a comment below with any question you might have

From all of us at North Lake Games, thank you for being on this journey with us. Let's paint the world yellow! 💛

Stay slimy!
Andreas Werdin

notes.title: May 2023 Update
notes.notes:
New trailer is out, which I spent way to much time working on. What do you think? I have also done lots of playtesting and some nice improvements to the game to prepare for the upcoming Steam Next Fest, which is the next big milestone I'm aiming for. I have also spent a lot of time with accessibility options since I want everyone to be able to play the game the way they want to. If you want you can check out the release notes below:

Demo Release notes

 Added 4 difficulty settings (easy, normal and 2 harder modes that unlock if finishing the game on previous difficulty). The different difficulties change player health, number of enemies per level and boss health.
 Holding fire buttons will fire weapon when reloaded (to avoid having to spam buttons)
 Autofire accessibility option - Makes your primary always fire when reloaded without player input required
 Possible to skip the gem box opening animation by pressing shoot-button
 Color rewards UX changes
 Changed so you have to click a button to interact with the Snail NPCs (instead of walking into them)
 Boss “The Queen and the Hive” added new attack and balancing to avoid spamming attacks
 New upgrade: Crossed Explosions - Makes Jelly Bomb, Slime Mines or Home Pillar explode in a large cross pattern
 New upgrade: Baseball Bat - Makes Splat Blade hit a small slime ball each swing
 New upgrade: Splat Yourself - Passive power upgrade that lets you spread splat around you every couple of seconds


Balancing changes
This is where I need your feedback the most. I'm completely blind to the difficulty, so please let me know if you feel the game is too easy or too hard, and also what gaming experience you have. This is the changes I have done based on recent playtests:

 Bee enemies movement speed increased
 Bee enemies fire delay decreased
 All primary weapons reload speed decreased
 Time between enemy respawns decreased
 1 more bee-enemy spawn each area on normal and easy difficulty
 Unlocked Hard & Ultra difficulty from the start in demo build


Bug fixes

 Fixed some audiobugs with music not turning off correctly
 Fixed bug that made it possible to trigger double amount of enemies in next area
 Fixed bug that made Splatterang deal a crazy amount of damage
 Fixed bug that game permanently could break if you remapped controls in certain ways (this fix needed all saved remappings to be reset, sorry about that)


What’s happening next? I am eagerly looking forward to the Steam Next Fest where I can hopefully get even more player feedback, and get ready for the final release. Im aiming for a Fall 2023 release at the moment, but let's see how that goes...

notes.title: April 2023 Update
notes.notes:
Main update of this month is that I just released a new, big update for the demo. Please check it out and let me know what you think. Those familiar with the previous version will hopefully see some nice upgrades. 
What's new?
New upgrade choices
Before you were presented with 3 options. Reward 1, Reward 2 or a Random Reward. I felt like something was missing, and the random reward felt… unpredictable and not really fun. I changed that so that now you will instead get 3 reward options right away. If you like none of them, you can instead get 50 coins to save for another time. If you already have some coins, you can spend 25 coins to reroll your 3 rewards to something else. The goal is to make the choices you make a bit more informed, while still allowing some influence of luck if you want to risk it. Let me know if you like the new version or the old one best.

New gem boxes
Before you got to choose between a standard reward or a random selection. Since the choice you were presented with didn't really help you make an informed choice, I removed it altogether. Instead I spiced up the reward box opening and split it in 3 tiers, and I think the end result is much nicer.

Better controller support
I have changed the input prompts to better work with controllers, so hopefully you will have a better experience using those now. I also added a title screen where I can check the users first button input and change your settings to either mouse or controller based on that. The title screen also helped improve performance when loading in the game since I can redirect you to the right area directly after that.

One thing to note is that I have been working on fixing some stuff in the save system, so your previous demo save (if you had any) will be reset. Sorry about that. As always, if you got any feedback, please share it either here in the steam forum or on youtube or any other place, I’m reading or watching almost all of it. Every bit of feedback helps!

Other news
Some other things I have worked on is of course polishing the game. I have quite a list of little bugs and  quirks I want to fix and improvements I want to add, so the more of that I have time to add before Steam Next Fest the better. Im also recording and editing a new trailer for that, which is a lot of fun but also takes soooo much time. Hopefully that will be live on my steam page very, very soon, and the you have to let me know what you think

notes.title: March 2023 Update
notes.notes:
Bad news: I’ve been on vacation and made slower than normal progress this month. Good news: The game is almost finished. So where are we at with it and when can you play the full thing?

What is done?

 The last boss, Princess Polka Dot, is done. A karate chopping lady bug high up in the treetops. Think she might be my most challenging but also favorite boss so far. What do you think of the name? Any other ideas?
 End credit scene: I wanted it to be satisfying for those of you who manage to reach the end so I have spent some time making a fun little cutscene for you all. I like it, so I hope you will too.
 Treetops content: I have been adding content in the form of fun rooms and more enemy types. Think this area is shaping up
 Bugs: I am playtasting like crazy and am still finding stuff, doing my best to fix it all before the launch.


What is not done?

 Before launch I have a couple of areas and bosses I want to polish up. I also plan to make sure to balance it as well as I can.
 Steam achievements. Not critical but I really want to have some, so working on adding a few ones.
 More upgrades and items. My idea list is still quite long and I have a couple I want to add for launch. I will have to draw the line somewhere and add the rest as future DLC, but a few more I think I can add.
 Testing… mentioned it above, but really want to have a smooth launch, so won’t try to rush it.


I have also signed up for Steam Next Fest in June, so I plan to release an improved version of the demo for that, and also prepare a stream where I play the full version of the game. Really excited about that.

notes.title: February 2023 Update
notes.notes:
Hey! Since the last update I have been working hard polishing and refining the game to make everything that happen after escaping the lawn much better. But since you won't be able to see that in the demo (yet), here comes a list of the improvements you CAN see:

New Weapons
I will admit, I might have started to go a bit crazy

 Freeze Ray - Lock slime in place so no scary bug can try to claim it later on. Frozen slime is forever yours. Great to combine with other weapons
 Machine Slime - Shoot three bullets in rapid succession to scare away even the bravest of bugs
 Splatterang - Throw a splatterang out in the wild and wait for it to return to you. Hard to master, but really powerful if you manage to reposition yourself fast
 Flying Star - To be honest, I don't know what the hell this is, I just had lots of fun with it after accidentally creating it
 Other Upgrades - Be able to have multiple primaries, reload weapons even when not on your turf, instant reloads, and new unique upgrades for a lot of the existing weapons.

Other things

 Fixed so many bugs that my head starts spinning... and I'm sure there is more, so keep reporting them. Splatting bugs has become my specialty now
 Added some new cool enemy types in the later areas... you dont want to face of against a Laser Wallflower or an Exploding Woodlouse
 Added more variation to the procedurally generated rooms


There is so much I want to add but I will try to keep next month super-focused to get the later areas closer to a finished state. No new weapons... or at least I'll try

notes.title: January 2023 Update
notes.notes:
Hey! Since releasing the demo I've gotten some great feedback from so many of you, and I have really been enjoying watching you spreading your turfs. I've gotten a much better sense of what works and in which areas the game can be improved. And I have been working hard making the game a lot better. So here is the release notes for the latest version of the demo:

Balancing changes
Main goal is to make the gameplay a bit faster and rewarding aggressive play-styles more

 Upped the aggression of many enemies by having them fly towards the player and attack
 Reduced cooldown of all primary weapons
 Increased the bullet speed of all shooting abilities and increased length of Frog Tongue and Splat Blade
 Reduced prize of in-run upgrades and unlocking of new starting weapons to allow for more experimentation
 Reduced speed boost effect of green slime (to not having your snail go complexity insane combining it with other abilities)

Quality of life & improvements

 Added an indicator on the gun when the primary weapon reloads
 Added confirmation messages if trying to dismiss rewards
 Added new upgrade type Indestructible Bullets (that can be combined with all other upgrades)
 Added more variation in room layouts

Bugs (not the enemy type)

 Fixed the button indicators to display correctectly no matter if you use controller or keyboard (based on your last input)
 Removed button remapping from the home base area due some errors reported (option still available from settings menu)
 Fixed in-run shop not working correct in some cases

At the same time I’m working on finishing one of the last areas of the game…The Treetops, featuring 8 new enemies, a new slime type, unique mechanics and obstacles and a nasty boss to finish it off. More will be revealed later, I promise
